title: Definition of serious adverse drug event incorporated by M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(c)
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(c) requires the manager of record of a pharmacy to report any serious adverse drug event, as defined in section 51H of chapter 111, occurring as a result of the patient's interaction with any drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy. Under M.G.L. c. 111, s. 51H(a), a serious adverse drug event is any untoward, preventable medical occurrence associated with the use of a drug in humans that results in any of the following outcomes: (i) death; (ii) a life-threatening outcome; (iii) inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization; (iv) a persistent or significant incapacity or substantial disruption of the ability to conduct normal life functions; (v) a congenital anomaly or birth defect; or (vi) any other kind of harm as determined by the department in regulation; provided, however, that adverse medical occurrences directly associated with the use of a drug in humans that may not immediately result in one of the outcomes listed in clauses (i) to (vi) may be considered a serious adverse drug event when they develop into or result in any of those outcomes. 247 CMR 2.00 contains no separate definition of the term.
exam_relevance: Tests that a serious adverse drug event under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(c), a term 247 CMR 20.02(2) also uses and 247 CMR 2.00 does not separately define, is defined by M.G.L. c. 111, s. 51H as an untoward, preventable medical occurrence associated with the use of a drug that results in one of the listed outcomes, so that a grave but unpreventable reaction is not one, and that an occurrence that later develops into a listed outcome may be considered one.

common_confusions: Treating every serious reaction to a drug as a serious adverse drug event, when M.G.L. c. 111, s. 51H requires an untoward, preventable medical occurrence that results in one of its listed outcomes.
Leaving out a congenital anomaly or birth defect, or any other kind of harm determined by the department in regulation, from the listed outcomes.

Treating an occurrence that does not immediately result in a listed outcome as outside the definition for good, when s. 51H provides that it may be considered a serious adverse drug event when it develops into or results in one.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-17 in the current text of M.G.L. c. 111, s. 51H(a) and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(c) on malegislature.gov, and in the current text of 247 CMR 2.00: Definitions published by the Board of Registration in Pharmacy on mass.gov, which defines no serious adverse drug event.
